name: Decimal expansion of the sum of the distinct entries of 1/A055204(n)^(1/2).
comment: A result of Erdős and Selfridge implies that A055204(n) only repeats at squares, so one can simply sum  1/A055204(n)^(1/2) for all n other than squares greater than 1. The number of elements of A387186 up to x is asymptotic to this constant times x^(1/2). Conjecturally, the same is true for A388851 (see also Erdős problem #374). The series converges at an exponentially fast rate.
link: Paul Erdős and Ron L. Graham, On products of factorials, Bull. Inst. Math. Acad. Sinica 4 (1976), pp. 337-355.
Terence Tao, Products of consecutive integers with unusual anatomy, arXiv:2603.27990 [math.NT], 2026. See p. 7 (Section 1.3).
